thread:
maya chen: quick sync — we need to pick a path for 'traffic-split rules' (customer req). do we ship API-first + minimal console controls, or full console UX at launch?

alvin park: API-first seems lower effort and matches our 'developer-first' story. go-to-market faster.

sophia liu: +1 on speed, but several enterprise customers asked explicitly for console controls and audit trail. missing that blocks sales.

maya chen: agreed. i'm trying to frame this as a prioritization problem: impact vs effort + sequencing. thoughts on using RICE to justify a phased approach?

eric wong: RICE helps. rough numbers: Reach = 30 (enterprises), Impact = 3 (blocks deals), Confidence = 0.6 (est), Effort = 8 wks for console. RICE = 30*3*0.6/8 = ~6.75. API-only effort = 2 wks, Impact = 2 (unblocks devs), gives RICE ~30*2*0.8/2 = 24.

maya chen: thanks eric — good to have ballpark. so API-first wins on score, but we need to capture sales blockers. options: 1) API-first with a 'console-lite' MVP (rules list, audit logs) in parallel, 2) API-only and ship a 'sales pack' (docs + PoC) while building console, 3) prioritize console and delay API improvements.

alvin park: option 1 sounds like more work but hedges risk. option 2 is lowest dev cost now but relies on SEs to close deals.

sophia liu: from PM + sales: option 2 is risky — we've seen deals stall waiting for UI. they want something they can demo.

maya chen: can we split scope: core runtime + API (routing, traffic weights, fallback) in sprint 1; console-lite (list + basic edit + audit trail) as a small sprint 2 that reuses API? that keeps dev flow and provides a demoable UI.

eric wong: technically feasible. dev effort estimate: runtime+API 2 engineers 2 wks, console-lite 1 engineer 3 wks. total sequenced ~5 wks.

alvin park: sounds reasonable. what's our launch criteria? (QA, perf SLOs, security review?)

maya chen: propose launch criteria: 1) API endpoints documented + stable, 2) console-lite with create/edit/list flows + audit log, 3) SLA: 95th < 120ms for control-plane ops in dedicated env, 4) integration test with canary route policy, 5) security review done.

sophia liu: add acceptance: sample demo script for sales + 1 customer pilot signoff.

maya chen: good. tradeoffs: more initial engineering overhead vs unlocking enterprise revenue sooner. propose we present RICE numbers + sequence plan at tomorrow PM sync and ask sales for two pilot accounts willing to test console-lite.

alvin park: +1. also add a fallback policy: if console work slips, ship API + a pre-built dashboard template SEs can use (low lift).

devex-bot: Reminder: New RFC template available at https://redwood.internal/rfcs — please attach design and rollout plan.

maya chen: thanks bot. i'll draft RFC with scores and acceptance criteria. will tag @sophia @alvin @eric for review before sync.

sophia liu: perfect. i'll pull sales notes for pilot accounts.

eric wong: will put up rough effort tickets and a CI smoke test for the canary flow.

alvin park: ok let's aim to finalize the plan by EOD today so we can get buy-in. :thumbsup:

maya chen: great — i'll post the RFC link once ready.

eric wong: one more note — consider telemetry budget: console users drive more control-plane ops; we should include a cost cap in the rollout plan.

maya chen: noted. include telemetry + quota recommendations in RFC.

sophia liu: thanks all — this feels actionable.

maya chen: closing the loop: action items in RFC: RICE table, sequencing plan, launch criteria, sales pilot list, telemetry/cost limits. will share for review.
